title: Divine Ethics · 2021 report · relevant selection
note: Fifteen relevant questions selected from the 20-question report tagged September 2021. The TestId 20146 report has the same 20 stems in a different order, with option variations; it is retained as a version, not another exam card. Five ambiguous or insufficiently supported items are excluded. Official I/II designation and sitting date remain unconfirmed. Answers are checked editorial study answers.
courseEvidence: Admitted by question-level comparison with the supplied review and first-term lessons, as requested. The original lacks a confirmed university I/II course code; content match is not a claim of official enrollment or syllabus completeness.
dateEvidence: Sitting date not established; no date is inferred from a download or Telegram posting.

audit.method: Source wording and option order checked against original pages/native text; answers compared with the current review, first-term notes and specified primary passages. Content relevance is not official course-code authentication. No official key is asserted.

questions.prompt: According to the Quran we should avoid much suspicion because:
options: It is harmful for our heart.
We can interpret it in a positive way.
It makes hatred among Muslims.
Some of it is sinful.
questions.note: Quran 49:12 explicitly gives sinfulness of some suspicions as the reason. This is the wording asked for, not a denial that suspicion can also damage relationships.

questions.prompt: What is the Islamic view about knowledge?
options: It is enough to merely accumulate information and data.
Contemplation is the best type of worship and reliance.
It is reading and memorizing facts.
It should be accompanied by reasoning and understanding.
questions.note: The first-term knowledge lesson emphasizes sound understanding rather than accumulation or memorization alone. The review p. 16 also joins reason with knowledge.
questions.reviewNote: Reason and knowledge guide ethical self-building; review p. 16.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to speak to God?
options: Only if we are alone can we speak loudly.
In case there are some people, we should find somewhere else to recite the Quran.
Neither speak in our prayers aloud nor in a low tone.
It is good to do it loudly.
questions.topic: Moderation and balance between faculties and duties
questions.note: The intended quotation is Quran 17:110: seek a middle way rather than either extreme of loudness or silence. The source option is an abbreviated translation, not a universal rule for every form of prayer.

options: Do not compare him/herself with those who are lower than him/her.
Humiliate him/herself to reach the position of best servant of God.
Do not compare him/herself with those who are lower than him/her.
Strengthen his/her understanding of profound need for God.
questions.note: Lesson 6, p. 13 directly gives D. A and C are duplicated in the original and remain duplicated here. Humility is not self-humiliation.

options: Is bad because it makes us lose control over words and actions.
Is good in case we harm those who attack us.
Should be balanced by being indifferent.
Is problematic if one never gets angry or is easily angered.
questions.note: The original stem is “Anger:”; a selection instruction is added for clarity. Lesson 7, p. 17 explicitly states the two extremes in D. A wrongly treats all anger as loss of control; the lesson allows appropriately regulated anger.

questions.prompt: The _____ level of the soul, which is _____, commands us to do bad things, and _____, which is the other level of the soul, blames us for doing something wrong.
options: Highest – al-nafs al-lawwamah – al-nafs al-ammarah.
Lowest – al-nafs al-ammarah – al-nafs al-lawwamah.
Lowest – al-nafs al-lawwamah – al-nafs al-ammarah.
Highest – al-nafs al-ammarah – al-nafs al-lawwamah.
questions.note: The commanding self is ammarah; the self-reproaching self is lawwamah. Quran 12:53 and 75:2 establish the names; “lowest” is the paper’s pedagogical ordering. The duplicated standalone question pasted above the original Q10 is an annotation, not an extra exam item.

questions.prompt: Who will be rewarded more than the martyrs?
options: The patient.
The merciful.
The modest.
The wise.
questions.topic: Moderation and balance between faculties and duties
questions.note: The intended trait is chastity/self-restraint (iffah), translated here as modesty, not shyness. Nahjul Balagha saying 474 compares the reward of one who can sin but remains chaste with the martyr. Its wording is “not greater than”, so the exam’s “more” is stronger than the cited saying; C remains the identifiable intended option.

questions.prompt: The only situation in which God tells us not to obey our parents is:
options: When they are enemies of God.
When they ask something wrong.
When they ask us to commit a sin.
When this thing is unacceptable.
questions.note: C is the precise intended principle: no obedience in wrongdoing. Quran 31:15 gives the case of pressure to associate partners with God while still requiring kind companionship. B can express the same principle if “wrong” means sinful, so B is also accepted for the source’s imprecise alternatives.

questions.prompt: Whoever saves one life, it is as if he has:
options: Served his lord in the best way.
Saved the lives of all people.
Served God on the day of resurrection.
Saved the lives of all his nation.
questions.topic: Forgiveness and good conduct toward others
questions.note: The comparison is with saving all humanity, Quran 5:32. The verse introduces this teaching as a decree for the Children of Israel. This is an ethical/scriptural question, not a clinical instruction.

questions.prompt: Purification of the soul according to the Quran brings:
options: Strengthening of the soul and prosperity.
Happiness and prosperity.
Piety and happiness.
Strengthening of the soul and discernment.
questions.note: B corresponds to falah (success/prosperity) in Quran 91:9 and the source’s translation. It is the intended scriptural outcome, not a guarantee of wealth or absence of distress.

questions.prompt: Which type of knowledge is necessary for everyone according to Islam?
options: Knowledge which helps us have a better life.
Knowledge which is necessary for society.
Knowledge which answers the basic and essential questions of everybody.
Knowledge which is responsible for the needs of the individual and society.
questions.note: The self-knowledge lesson begins with fundamental questions about identity, origin, destination and purpose. C is the most specific match to those essential questions, rather than every field needed by society.
questions.reviewNote: Identity, origin, destination and purpose are the guiding questions on review p. 16.

questions.prompt: In addition to telling the truth, we should believe in the truth, accept the truth, and:
options: Trust the truth.
Avoid lies.
Understand the truth.
Commit ourselves to the truth.
questions.note: Lesson 8, p. 19 requires compliance with truth in action as well as speech and belief. D completes that progression.

questions.prompt: What is the connection between business and remembrance of God according to the Quran?
options: We should do all the necessary activities and at the same time remember God.
The best way is to divide our time for both equally and have dunya and hereafter.
Being busy with dunya is against remembrance of God, so we should detach from dunya.
It is better to reduce business and be busy with God to be close to Him.
questions.topic: Moderation and balance between faculties and duties
questions.note: Lesson 4, p. 9 quotes Quran 24:37 about trade not distracting from remembrance. Responsible daily work and inward awareness coexist; the review also says time allocations need not be equal.
questions.reviewNote: Work, worship and rest are balanced by needs and priorities, not necessarily equal durations, review pp. 4–5.

questions.prompt: Who are excellent companions whom God has blessed according to the Quran?
options: The prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, the righteous.
Imams, the truthful, the martyrs, the righteous.
True Muslims, the truthful, the faithful, the righteous.
The prophets, the faithful, the martyrs, the righteous.
questions.note: Quran 4:69 names these four groups. This exact list is not printed in the current review, so the primary verse is linked instead of a substitute review section.

questions.prompt: _____ is a form of resistance against problems which _____.
options: Patience – helps one continue toward goals despite all the challenges one may face.
Satisfaction – helps one continue toward goals despite all the challenges one may face.
Satisfaction – one should withstand it to achieve perfection despite all the challenges.
Patience – makes one indifferent and tolerate the situation until matters resolve.
questions.note: Lesson 9, pp. 21–22 defines active, regulated perseverance. Patience is neither indifference nor merely waiting for circumstances to resolve themselves.
